methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $6.0B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Drones & Autonomous. Range: $3.3B - $8.6B.

data.narrative:
Nuro, a Series G autonomous delivery drone company founded by Dave Ferguson and Jiajun Zhu, commands a current post-money valuation of $6.0B on $2.54B raised to date. The valuation is assessed against a peer universe of 6 private frontier-tech companies in the Drones & Autonomous sector, including later-stage players like Wayve ($8.6B, Series D), Zipline ($7.6B, Series H), and public comparables Joby Aviation ($6.9B) and Archer Aviation ($3.3B).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-Progression analysis applies a typical 1.25x step-up multiplier to the $6.0B last post-money valuation, implying $7.5B at the next funding round. Peer-Median analysis across the four primary comparables (Wayve, Zipline, Joby, Archer) yields a median valuation of $7.2B, with a range spanning $3.3B to $8.6B. This peer set reflects similar valuation tier and sector exposure.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $6.1B to $8.6B, with a median of $7.4B. The current $6.0B valuation sits at the lower bound, consistent with typical post-money pricing. Key uncertainties include near-term commercialization progress, regulatory clarity on autonomous delivery operations, and relative competitive positioning within the peer cohort, where valuations span a wide 2.6x spread.
